ruling.recommended_action: Close the case as no refund: no exempt/chargeable finding changes the fixed fare, and the off-route segment is excused by the rider's prior agreement. No account flag is warranted (no non-exempt segment).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeX fixed-quote trip (F6), so the fare does not vary with distance; the trace's RD-2 check fails because a fixed fare means detour kilometres do not enter the charge [F4][F6][RD-2]. The refundable amount is therefore $0.00: $23.91 ÷ 16.96 km = $1.4098/km, but there is no exempt/chargeable split that alters a fixed quote, so no money moves [F4][F6][RD-2]. The only live question is whether the single off-route segment is excuseable, which matters only for the RD-6 account flag because the driver has prior upheld route disputes (F17) [F3][F17][RD-1][RD-6].

On the segment: the driver asked before turning off and named a road — "Jam on Pan Island Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Bedok Reservoir Road?" at 09:45 (F7) — and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead." at 09:46 (F8), i.e. a rider message sent before the segment started (09:49, F3) agreeing to a specific named road [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. The corroborating LTA speed band on the PIE (band 2, 10–19 km/h) is consistent with the claim of congestion, though a band alone does not exempt (RD-4(b)) and no incident was recorded (F11, F14) [F11][F14][RD-4]. The record does not tie the driven path to Bedok Reservoir Road by any road name in the fact table, and the driver's own post-trip statement also names Bedok Reservoir Road, so the record does not place the segment somewhere else either (F10) [F10][RD-5]. The agreement is therefore a specific named-road consent whose correspondence to the driven segment is untied: under the trace's rule for RD-5, nothing ties the segment to the named road and nothing places it elsewhere, which is undetermined, not exempt and not a driver's errand of his own [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. A driver's claim of agreement appearing only in his statement is not consent (G11), but here the rider's own timestamped chat message supplies it (F8, F9) [F8][F9][RD-5].

That finding is not dispositive for a flag: an undetermined finding means escalation only when it changes the amount or the flag. The amount is fixed and unchanged (F6) whether the segment is exempt or not [F6][RD-2]; and since the segment is a rider-agreed route choice, not an unexplained deviation, no non-exempt segment is established against the driver, so the RD-6 precondition (a refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) is not met and no account flag is warranted even though a prior upheld dispute exists (F17) [F17][RD-1][RD-6]. With the fare fixed and no open question that changes the outcome, I can leave the tie undetermined and still rule: the complaint of an unexplained longer route does not produce a refund on a fixed quote [F4][F6][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read the chat (F7, F8), the driver's statement (F10) and the complaint; nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence: the chat record is complete and timestamped (F9), the segment is measured (F3) and the fare breakdown is present (F6), so the record settles every element this ruling needs [F3][F6][F9].

The driver-side 'no_action' request matches the outcome, but his justification rests on his post-trip statement (F10), which alone would not be consent (G11); the ruling instead relies on the rider's timestamped chat message (F8) and leaves the segment undetermined rather than exempt, so no account flag is triggered [F8][F10][RD-5][RD-6].
